description: The OUTS shared-memory section: the processed frame a third-party consumer (OBS via Spout2, a ReShade add-on, a recorder) can attach to. The section identifies itself by a marker header so a consumer never guesses from the name.

section.naming: NeuralScreenOut_<pid>_<suffix> (the name changes on every open; discover via the worker's stdout protocol or the config)

layout_v1.offset_0: uint64 seqlock - odd while the worker writes, even when the frame is complete (torn-frame detection)
layout_v1.offset_32: width * height * 4 bytes - the frame, row-major, top-down, RGBA order

section.tearing: Copy under the seqlock: read seq (must be even), copy, re-read seq; if it changed or went odd, retry (a few times), then skip the frame.
section.compatibility: The marker and the frame are written under ONE seqlock, so a consumer that checks the sequence never sees a torn header. Version bumps change the header's version field first; a consumer that does not know the version must not read past offset 12.

channels.spout2: the same pixels published as a Spout2 shared texture (set 'spout' in config.json or RECORDING -> Spout2 output) - OBS's Spout2 Capture plugin consumes it directly
